The Ag complex ensemble contains a separate molecule next to the complex; the Ru complex is a single
molecule whose weakest metal–ligand contact can be cut by lowering the bonding buffer.

**Files used** (from the repository):

* `files/ensemble.xyz` — 18 conformers of an Ag complex, 168 atoms
* `files/opt.out` — ORCA, r²SCAN-3c OptTS Freq (transition state), Ru complex C45H42F3IO2P2Ru (96 atoms)

**1. Fragments of every conformer** (default buffer 0.3 Å).

```bash
frog-fragments files/ensemble.xyz
```

```text

         Fragments (files/ensemble.xyz)
╭───────────┬─────────────┬─────────────────────╮
│ Conformer │ N Fragments │ Atom Indices        │
├───────────┼─────────────┼─────────────────────┤
│         0 │           2 │ 0:11 50:167 | 12:49 │
│         1 │           2 │ 0:11 50:167 | 12:49 │
│         2 │           2 │ 0:11 50:167 | 12:49 │
│         3 │           2 │ 0:11 50:167 | 12:49 │
│         4 │           2 │ 0:11 50:167 | 12:49 │
│         5 │           2 │ 0:11 50:167 | 12:49 │
│         6 │           2 │ 0:11 50:167 | 12:49 │
…
```

Every conformer (only the first 7 rows are shown) has the same two fragments: atoms 0–11 plus 50–167
(the Ag complex) and atoms 12–49 (a separate 38-atom molecule). Use these ranges for `-E` in
`frog-steric` or `--fragment` in other commands.

**2. Smaller buffer on the Ru complex, and write each fragment** (`-w`) to its own folder.

```bash
frog-fragments files/opt.out -b 0.1 -w --out-dir frags
```

```text

Ru complex `files/opt.out` (rendered with xyzrender, hydrogens hidden). Highlighted in magenta are the atoms of fragment 1 found with `-b 0.1`.
```

With the default buffer (0.3 Å) the Ru complex is one fragment (see the table above for the Ag
complex). With `-b 0.1` the 7-atom unit `41 49:53 95` (O, C, C, three F and H, shown in the file)
is no longer bonded to the rest of the complex. The other fragment (atoms 0–40, 42–48 and 54–94)
keeps the Ru atom (36). Both are written to `frags/`.
